An evaluator that researches livelihoods charities and recommends the most cost-effective ones to donors. Ambitious Impact published one public model of its work; the most recent, from February 2025, puts it at **<span data-figure="headline" data-model="better-futures-guide-aim">63</span> years of healthy life per $1,000**.

| Model | By | Date | Years of healthy life per $1,000 | Cells reproduced |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Better Futures Guide: a livelihoods charity evaluator (Ambitious Impact, 2025 idea report)](/better-futures-guide) | AIM | February 2025 | <span data-figure="headline" data-model="better-futures-guide-aim">63</span> | 168, 14 kept fixed |

**Purely theoretical.** Ambitious Impact's estimate is of the idea, written before Better Futures Guide existed, not of the charity's own results. It is shown because Better Futures Guide runs the programme today ([checked October 2026](https://betterfuturesguide.org/)) and no model of its actual work exists yet.

**Where we differ from Ambitious Impact.** Better Futures Guide works through the money it moves or redirects, not a programme of its own, so our view values each such dollar the way the site values every meta charity's: by GiveWell's Top Charities, each at its live result on this site, so the sliders move it too. Half the money is counted as new; the rest only for the gain over GiveDirectly. A new organisation's chance of success is the site's shared 56%. Ambitious Impact's own valuation stays in the evaluator view. [How money moved is valued](https://github.com/heychristoph/charityevals/blob/main/docs/normalization.md#28-money-moved-success-and-career-changes-one-method-october-2026).
